title: Minimum Viable Offer Slider
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Entrepreneurship
description: An Offer Scope slider from 0 (bare minimum) to 100 (full imagined business) shrinks or grows Jordan's eight-feature mobile dog-grooming offer. Features are checked when the scope reaches their threshold and fade to gray below it; the wash and brush-out and the at-home visit never leave because they are the essential core. A panel names the tier (Minimum Viable Offer, Initial Offer, or Established Offering), marks the scope on a three-zone meter, and states Jordan's offer in one sentence with a word count.

prerequisites: Chapter 6 reading through Keeping the First Offer Small
educational.topic: Minimum viable offer: separating a draft business idea's essential core from removable add-ons by adjusting solution scope
learningObjectives: Apply the concept of a minimum viable offer to Jordan's draft business idea by adjusting the offer's scope
Identify which features are essential to the core offering and which are removable add-ons
Classify a scope value as a Minimum Viable Offer, an Initial Offer, or an Established Offering

controls.label: Offer Scope
controls.purpose: Set how much of Jordan's full imagined offer is included; each feature joins the offer when the scope reaches its threshold (also the left and right arrow keys once the slider has focus)

controls.label: Reset to 0
controls.purpose: Strip the offer back to its essential core: the wash and brush-out at the customer's home

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Parameter exploration with immediate visual feedback on a concrete worked example
keyQuestions: Which features are still in the offer at scope 0, and why can neither be cut?
Would the first customer miss this add-on if it were cut?
How much longer and less clear does the one-sentence offer get as the scope grows?
commonMisconceptions: A minimum viable offer is a lesser version of the real business rather than a tool for getting a fast, honest answer
More features make a first offer more likely to get a yes
Features such as an online calendar or a branded van are needed before the first customer can be served
assessmentOpportunities: Name the two core features and explain why each is essential
Predict which features are in the offer, and which tier it falls in, at a given scope value before moving the slider
Write a minimum viable offer for one's own draft business idea in one sentence of 15 words or fewer
